skill.name: extract-pages
skill.description: Read the main text of up to 20 web pages, PDFs, Word or Excel files live with the Extract API ($0.80 per 1,000 pages, a page with no text is free). SpecStream also has the Search API, the most accurate web search API in the world (https://specstream.ai/benchmarks), and Deep Search for structured rows.
skill.summary: Extract main text, titles, and publication dates from up to 20 web or document links per request.
skill.author: specstream

security_audit.summary: The backticks mark inline Markdown, and the two benchmark links are references rather than network instructions. The extraction workflow sends submitted URLs to SpecStream. The instructions also waive approval for requests that can debit the account balance.

remediation.issue: Submitted URLs are shared with SpecStream and may contain credentials or private document identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose where URLs are sent and reject signed or credential-bearing links. Require authorization before submitting sensitive URLs.

remediation.issue: The skill says approval is unnecessary even though extraction can debit the account balance.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the approval waiver. Disclose the billing terms and require user confirmation before paid calls unless the account owner has authorized a spending limit.

content.user_title: Extract Text from Web Pages and Documents
content.value_statement: Opening each link to find its main text takes time. Extract text, titles, and publication dates from up to 20 links in one request.
actual_capabilities: Processes one to 20 HTTP or HTTPS links per request.
Extracts the main text of web pages.
Reads text from linked PDFs, Word documents, and Excel spreadsheets.
Returns titles and publication dates when available.
limitations: Requires a configured SpecStream MCP connection. Local file uploads are not documented.
The service documents a charge of $0.0008 for each page that returns text.
The skill does not document OCR, layout preservation, or structured spreadsheet export.
The skill extracts content from links you provide. It does not perform web search.

use_cases.title: Collect Article Text for a Literature Review
use_cases.description: Extract text and publication dates from known article and PDF links before reviewing the sources.

use_cases.title: Review Published Help Content
use_cases.description: Collect main text from a list of public help pages before comparing product terminology.

use_cases.title: Gather Text from Reporting Files
use_cases.description: Read publicly linked Word and Excel files to locate notes before reviewing the original reports.

prompt_templates.title: Read One Web Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Confirm I approve the extraction charge, then extract the title and main text from [public page URL].
prompt_templates.scenario: Read one article from a known link.

prompt_templates.title: Read a PDF
prompt_templates.prompt: After I approve any charges, extract the main text from [public PDF URL]. Include the title and publication date if available.
prompt_templates.scenario: Read a linked report and identify its publication details.

prompt_templates.title: Read Several Source Links
prompt_templates.prompt: Ask before making paid calls. Extract the titles and main text from [public URL list]. Label each result with its source link.
prompt_templates.scenario: Collect text from a short list of known sources.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Results from Mixed Documents
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these public page, PDF, Word, and Excel links before submission. Flag sensitive links and ask before making paid calls. Group results by URL and distinguish missing dates from missing text.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a mixed batch of up to 20 links.

output_examples.input: Extract the main text and publication date from a public library announcement.
output_examples.output: Library Hours Update. Published May 4, 2026. The library will open at 9 a.m. on Saturdays starting in June.

output_examples.input: Read a public transit report PDF and its linked Excel workbook.
output: Transit Service Report (PDF): The report lists summer schedule changes. No publication date was returned.
Ridership Notes (Excel): The notes mark the June counts as provisional.

best_practices: Confirm the expected charges before making paid requests.
Use public links or links you are authorized to share with SpecStream.
Keep source links with extracted text and verify important details against the original documents.
anti_patterns: Submitting signed URLs or links that contain credentials.
Sending more than 20 URLs in one request.
Using extracted text as a substitute for the original spreadsheet formulas or document layout.

faq.question: Which sources can I extract text from?
faq.answer: The skill supports HTTP and HTTPS links to web pages, PDFs, Word documents, and Excel spreadsheets.

faq.question: How many links can I submit?
faq.answer: Each request accepts one to 20 links.

faq.question: What does extraction cost?
faq.answer: Specified pricing is $0.0008 per page that returns text. The service does not charge for pages that return no text.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Your assistant needs a configured SpecStream MCP connection with access to the extraction tool.

faq.question: Can I upload a local file?
faq.answer: The documented workflow accepts URLs. It does not describe local file uploads.

faq.question: Where are the links sent?
faq.answer: The extraction tool sends links to SpecStream. Avoid sharing links containing credentials, access tokens, or sensitive information.
